title: JSON Tables
tagline: Turns JSON-shaped data into relational tables.
role: exapump loads CSV and Parquet; a JSON document is an arbitrarily nested tree, and this add-on shreds it into tables. exakit data-load installs it for you the moment you hand it a .json file - it asks nothing, and one document may legitimately produce several tables.
installed_by: Automatically by exakit data-load when you load a JSON file, or from exakit marketplace.
platforms: macOS and Linux (including WSL). Not available on Windows: the ingest engine cannot be wired in there.

quickstart.note: Pick the file, give it SCHEMA.TABLE, and the engine is installed and run for you.

commands.summary: The normal way in - hand it a .json file.
Shred JSON into Parquet by hand.

notes: The ingest engine ships PREBUILT. Nobody needs Rust or cargo - never tell a user to install a toolchain.
Several tables from one document all land in the schema you named, sharing the table name you gave as their prefix.

troubleshooting.symptom: exapump will not take my .json file
troubleshooting.remedy: That is expected - use exakit data-load, which routes JSON through this add-on.

troubleshooting.symptom: No tables came out of the document
troubleshooting.remedy: Check the file really is JSON or NDJSON, then retry exakit data-load.
Windows cannot run the engine. Load the file from macOS, Linux or WSL.
